title: Neither the invoice format library nor the KoSIT validator holds the approval of a low-confidence extraction
content:
The e-invoicing stack divides cleanly and stops short of the decision. Mustangproject solves the format half — reading, writing and validating the document. The KoSIT validator computes an acceptance status. Neither of them holds the approval: who accepted a low-confidence extraction, under which rule, at what time.

The qualifier "low-confidence" is what makes this a real gap rather than a theoretical one. For a clean invoice, format conformance and acceptance are the same event and no human is involved. For an ambiguous one, someone overrides or confirms a machine judgement, and that override is the only part of the chain with a person's name attached to it — and the part neither component retains.

The stakes come from the regime rather than the software: under clearance, an incorrect submission is a filed tax document, not a draft. There is no revision step in which the mistake is merely internal. Two German leads carry this finding, one of them the maintainer of the format library itself, which makes the division of labour a shared premise rather than a criticism.
